title: Establish request-fidelity bands and graceful triage procedure for endpoints
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Define a pragmatic, per-endpoint framework that declares request-fidelity bands (high/medium/low) and an associated graceful triage procedure to guide multi-region failover, dynamic circuit breakers, and load-shedding decisions. This ticket codifies how we translate observable SLIs into a bounded set of operational outcomes (traffic keep, soft-throttle, hard-evict, regional redirect) and the error-budget accounting that triggers each outcome.
background: We operate routes with widely varying quality requirements: some conversational routes are latency-sensitive and quality-critical for user retention; others are batch embeddings or low-fidelity reranking where degraded output is acceptable temporarily. Existing SLO docs across the org enumerate SLIs and per-endpoint SLOs, but there's no concise mechanism to map measured SLI drift into deterministic actions across regions and model variants. This gap has led to inconsistent failover behavior and ad-hoc throttles during incidents. The request-fidelity bands project aims to create a small, operationalizable policy surface that engineers and SREs can use to configure deterministic degradation behaviors while preserving predictability for customers.
proposal: Introduce three request-fidelity bands: HIGH (retain full model variant, strict latency SLO >= 99th percentile threshold), MEDIUM (allow quantized/cheaper variant, modest latency allowance), LOW (fallback to cached responses, stub responses, or enqueue for async processing). For each band, define: 1) SLI thresholds (latency p95/p99, error-rate, quality-regression alerting with promptset evals); 2) Error budget burn ladders (soft throttle at 25% burn, hard throttle at 75% burn); 3) Circuit behavior (per-region open/half-open logic, backoff windows, failover targets). Policies are parameterized per-endpoint via a compact manifest: fidelity_band, primary_variant, fallback_variants, regional_priority, kb_cache_policy. We'll provide a validator and a Helm chart fragment for Dedicated and Private deployments so the same policy runs across modes.
acceptance_criteria: A concise fidelity-band manifest spec exists in the repo (YAML schema) and is checked by CI
Runtime accepts manifest and exposes decisions in tracing/span tags (fidelity.band, decision.reason, target.variant)
Simulated canary in staging exercises all three bands with injected latency and KC cache misses; results documented and pass acceptance thresholds
Runbook entries created for SREs describing triage steps for soft vs hard throttle and regional redirect
Dashboard panel in Console shows per-endpoint fidelity band, current error-budget burn rate, and predicted time-to-throttle
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Implement manifest spec and validator; unit tests + CI linting (2 weeks)
Phase 1: Runtime integration: expose decision tags and a feature flag to enable band-driven behavior in staging (3 weeks)
Phase 2: Staged rollout to low-traffic endpoints in hosted (canary) and Dedicated non-production pools (2 weeks)
Phase 3: Gradual expansion to high-traffic endpoints with post-rollout monitoring and a 72-hour observation window (4 weeks)
Phase 4: Document playbook and handoff to SRE/operational readiness (1 week)
monitoring_signals: Availability: 5xx rate and client-visible error rate
Quality: periodic promptset eval regression delta and hallucination score (where applicable)
Error-budget burn: windowed burn-rate (1h, 6h, 24h) with projection
Circuit state: per-region circuit open/closed/half-open metrics and last-transition timestamp
